key_facts: Coalition of Canadian media organisations sued Anthropic and its Canadian subsidiary in Ontario Superior Court
Filed on 6 Oct 2026; first reported by CARTT.ca, a sister publication of Broadcast Dialogue
Plaintiffs: Toronto Star, The Globe and Mail, Metroland Media, Postmedia Network and PNI Maritimes LP, and The Canadian Press
Allege systematic scraping of millions of works to train and operate Claude without permission or payment, including bypassing paywalls
Seek damages possibly in the billions, statutory damages up to $20,000 per work, and injunctions
The Canadian Press owns the most works allegedly scraped (4.2 million)
Anthropic has not yet filed a defence; foreign defendants have up to 60 days under Ontario rules
quote_evidence: A coalition of Canadian media organizations has launched a sweeping legal action in Ontario Superior Court against AI developer Anthropic and its Canadian subsidiary, alleging ongoing unauthorized scraping of its copyrighted journalism.
Anthropic has not yet filed a statement of defence.
why_it_matters_hint: Another major copyright claim against an AI developer, from the news industry.
notes: Lawsuit filed 6 Oct, before the window; reported 14 Oct. Allegations only.
title: Canadian news publishers sue Anthropic over AI copyright infringement
